THOUGHT: This 67-year-old male presents with asymmetric, episodic knee swelling and pain (right knee currently active, left knee recently involved), improvement with rest, functional limitation, and concomitant chronic back pain with reduced spinal mobility. His long-standing arthritis diagnosis (16 years) initially suggests osteoarthritis (OA), but several features challenge a simple OA diagnosis: (1) the *inflammatory* nature of the current presentation—swelling, warmth, tenderness, elevated ESR and CRP—contrasts with typical non-inflammatory OA; (2) the *migratory, asymmetric pattern* (left knee improved, right now active) is atypical for primary OA, which is usually chronic, progressive, and bilateral/symmetric; (3) negative RF and anti-CCP make rheumatoid arthritis unlikely; (4) X-ray shows joint space narrowing and subchondral sclerosis—consistent with OA—but importantly *no erosions*, further arguing against RA or other erosive arthropathies; (5) spine X-ray shows only mild degenerative changes, no sacroiliitis—making ankylosing spondylitis or other spondyloarthropathies less likely; (6) the presence of dandruff and nail pitting is highly suggestive of *psoriasis*—a common comorbidity in psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Nail pitting is a well-recognized cutaneous marker of PsA, present in up to 80% of PsA patients with nail involvement. Though the patient doesn’t report overt skin plaques, scalp psoriasis (manifesting as refractory dandruff) is common and often underrecognized. The combination of inflammatory oligoarticular arthritis (asymmetric, migratory, lower-limb dominant), nail pitting, dandruff (scalp psoriasis), elevated acute-phase reactants, and absence of RF/anti-CCP strongly supports psoriatic arthritis over other spondyloarthropathies or OA. While he has longstanding “arthritis,” it may have been undiagnosed PsA all along—or OA coexisting with PsA—but the acute inflammatory flare with systemic markers and extra-articular features points to PsA as the driver of the current presentation.

DIAGNOSIS: Psoriatic arthritis
